acts.title: Nine minutes, thirty-nine kilometres
text: On 14 October 2012 an Austrian skydiver called Felix Baumgartner became the first person to travel faster than the speed of sound without an engine. Eight million people watched it live.

The morning did not go smoothly. The team cancelled the first attempt because of the wind, and Baumgartner sat in the capsule for two hours before anybody told him anything. At 9.30 the balloon finally took off. It lifted him slowly — it took two and a half hours to reach 39,000 metres, which is roughly four times higher than a passenger plane flies.

Then he opened the door, stood on the step and jumped. For the first thirty seconds everything went to plan. After that he began to turn round and round, faster and faster, and for a few seconds the people watching thought the jump had failed. He did not panic. He waited, moved his arms, and the spinning stopped.

He pulled the parachute at 1,500 metres and landed on his feet in the New Mexico desert nine minutes and three seconds after he left the capsule. The rescue team reached him a minute later. He was already standing up.
Asked afterwards what he thought about at 39,000 metres, he said he was not thinking about records. He was thinking about going home.

tts: Hello, and welcome to Making History, the programme where we look back at human achievements that have changed history.
It was on the fourteenth of October 2012 that Felix Baumgartner, a pilot from Austria, made history when he became the first person to go faster than the speed of sound.
Eight million people watched live on YouTube as Baumgartner made the amazing jump out of a balloon from a height of thirty-eight kilometres above the Earth.
Baumgartner’s journey started at 3.16 p.m., when the large balloon slowly lifted him into the sky.

items.s: He was the first person to go faster than the speed of sound.
Eight million people watched it live.

write.q: Tell a true past event in sequence: 6 sentences. Use First, Then, After that and In the end, at least four past verbs (two of them irregular), and one negative with didn’t.
write.model: Last summer I climbed a mountain for the first time. First we took a bus to the village at four in the morning. Then we started walking, and after two hours I understood that my shoes were wrong. After that it began to rain and we didn’t see anything from the top. In the end we came down in the dark and ate everything in the first café we found. It took eleven hours and I would do it again.

speak.q: Tell the Baumgartner story out loud in five sentences, in order. Then tell one true past event of your own in three sentences.
speak.model: First the balloon took off at half past nine. It lifted him for two and a half hours. Then he jumped from 39,000 metres. After that he began to spin, but he didn’t panic. In the end he landed safely after nine minutes.
